metaTitle: Best Bluetooth Tracker Cards for Wallets (2026)
metaDescription: Six card-shaped Bluetooth trackers for wallets compared on thickness, battery type, ring volume and iPhone or Android support, so you can pick the right one.
introParagraphs: A tracker card is the answer to a wallet that a bulky key tag cannot join. It is shaped like a credit card, slides into a slot beside your real cards and rings from your phone when the wallet goes missing. Because you carry it every day, thickness and battery routine matter more here than they do for a keychain tag.

We evaluated six card trackers based on product specs and buyer feedback. Four are rechargeable, one is a sealed non-rechargeable card with a very long claimed life, and one lists a battery of 5 to 10 years. Three are iPhone only and three work with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub.
Check thickness and charging first, since those decide whether the card actually lives in your wallet.

products.name: The Ridge Tracker Card

specList.label: Networks
specList.value: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

specList.label: Ringer
specList.value: Up to 95 dB, range up to 300 ft

products.description:
The Ridge Tracker Card is the most complete wallet card here because it works with both phone worlds and publishes clear numbers. You can use Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, and the listing says the ringer reaches up to 95 dB with a range of up to 300 feet in open areas. It recharges on any Qi or MagSafe charger and the 155 mAh battery is rated for up to 5 months per charge.

Proximity alerts tell you when the wallet moves out of range, and you can ask Siri to locate it or view it on a map. An IP68 rating covers splashes and spills. The tradeoff is the 5-month charge, which is shorter than several rivals, and the listing suggests placing the card under a cash strap or money clip for best performance.

It asks you to charge it a couple of times a year. At up to 5 months per charge it needs power more often than the Chipolo CARD at up to a year, but it works on both networks and carries IP68, which the Chipolo does not state. Next to the SPOTMINDERS card at 100 dB it rings softer.
products.bestFor: Wallet carriers who want a rated-waterproof card on either phone type.

products.name: UGREEN FineTrack Slim Wallet Tracker Card

specList.label: Charge
specList.value: 20 minutes for up to a year

products.description:
The UGREEN FineTrack Slim is the card for iPhone owners who want the smallest charging routine. The listing says just 20 minutes of charging powers it for up to a full year, which is among the longest rechargeable claims here. It pairs with a press of the function button for 2 to 3 seconds and then follows the Find My prompts.

Tapping Play Sound in Find My triggers a loud 100 dB alert, and the app sends a notification with the last known location when the card moves out of range. Lost Mode lets you leave contact details. The tradeoff is that it is iOS only, the listing does not state a water rating, and it supports iPhone and iPad on iOS 14.5 or later and Mac on macOS 11 or later.

It is a card you charge once a year and forget. At up to a year per charge it outlasts the Ridge at up to 5 months, and it rings at 100 dB against the Ridge's 95 dB, but it has no IP68 claim and no Android option. Compared with the Chipolo CARD it also lacks Find Hub.
products.bestFor: iPhone owners who want a card that charges quickly and lasts a year.

products.name: Chipolo CARD Wallet Tracker

specList.label: Networks
specList.value: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

specList.label: Shape
specList.value: Thin card for wallets and passports

products.description:
The Chipolo CARD is the card with the clearest support promise. It works with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, so Android owners are covered, and the listing describes a streamlined slim body for wallets, passport pouches and IDs. You ring it from the app to find a wallet hidden nearby, or check the map when it is farther away.

The battery recharges on a Qi magnetic wireless charger and lasts up to a year on one charge. The listing states the charger is not included, which is the main gotcha. It also gives no ring volume or water rating. Chipolo adds a 2-year warranty and a free replacement through the seller if anything goes wrong.

The once-a-year charge is a light routine. At up to a year per charge it lasts longer than the Ridge at up to 5 months and matches the UGREEN Slim, and unlike the UGREEN it works on Android. Against the KIUP card at 120 dB it publishes no loudness, but it is the one with a stated warranty.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a dual-network card with a stated 2-year warranty.

products.name: BFADEHA Wallet Tracker Smart Card

specList.label: Network
specList.value: Apple Find My, MFi, iOS only

products.description:
The BFADEHA is the only card here that skips charging entirely. The listing says it is non-rechargeable and built to last over 5 years, with no cables or wireless pad needed. It is Apple MFi certified, uses a standard credit-card form factor and is 2.5 mm thick, so it fits any wallet slot.

A 100 dB speaker rings through Find My, and intelligent left-behind alerts warn you if you leave the wallet in a taxi or restaurant. Setup is a one-tap pairing with the iPhone. The tradeoff is that it is iOS only and, once the sealed battery is gone, you replace the whole card. The listing gives no water rating.

It suits someone who hates charging. Against the Ridge, which needs a pad and a recharge every 5 months, it asks nothing, and at 2.5 mm it is a little thicker than the SPOTMINDERS at about 0.07 inches. Compared with the KIUP card it has a shorter claimed life and no Android support.

products.name: SPOTMINDERS Wallet Tracker PRO Card

specList.label: Network
specList.value: Apple Find My, MFi, iOS only

products.description:
The SPOTMINDERS PRO is an iPhone-only card designed to look like an ordinary credit card. It is Apple MFi certified, rated IP68 and about 0.07 inches thick, so it blends into a wallet or passport sleeve. The listing says the rechargeable battery gives up to 8 months of use per charge and is designed to last over 5 years.

A 100 dB speaker rings through Find My, you can ask Siri to find the wallet hands-free, and left-behind alerts help with taxis and restaurants. It recharges using wireless charging. The tradeoff is iOS only compatibility and an 8-month charge cycle that comes around more often than the UGREEN Slim's year.

It sits between the Ridge and the UGREEN on battery. At up to 8 months it beats the Ridge's 5 months, but the Ridge works on Android too, and the UGREEN Slim lasts longer on a 20 minute charge. Next to the BFADEHA it has an IP68 rating the BFADEHA does not state.

products.name: KIUP Wallet Tracker Card

specList.label: Networks
specList.value: Google Find Hub and Apple Find My

products.description:
The KIUP card makes the biggest claims in this group. The listing says it works with both Google Find Hub and Apple Find My, rings up to 120 dB, carries an IP68 rating and measures 0.06 inches thin. It states a battery life of 5 to 10 years on both Android and iOS devices.

A UWB distance view within Bluetooth range shows how close the card is. The listing says it is not for GPS use and not for Huawei phones. The tradeoff is that its 5 to 10 year battery claim is a manufacturer number you should treat cautiously, and the listing does not say whether the battery can be recharged or replaced.

It is the loudest card here. At 120 dB it rings louder than the Ridge at 95 dB and the SPOTMINDERS at 100 dB, and it works on Android where those iPhone cards do not. Compared with the Chipolo CARD it has no warranty described, so the brand's claims rely on buyer feedback.
products.bestFor: Shoppers who want the loudest, thinnest card on either phone network.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A card that makes your wallet bulge defeats the point. The KIUP lists 0.06 inches, the SPOTMINDERS 0.07 inches, and the BFADEHA 2.5 mm. A standard credit card is about 0.8 mm, so every tracker card is several times thicker. Test it in your wallet slot before relying on it. If you carry many cards, favor the thinner listings.

Cards charge in different ways. The Ridge needs a Qi or MagSafe pad every 5 months, the SPOTMINDERS every 8 months, and the Chipolo CARD and UGREEN Slim about once a year. The BFADEHA is non-rechargeable at over 5 years, and the KIUP claims 5 to 10 years. Fewer charges means less upkeep, but a sealed battery means replacing the card eventually.

A card must talk to your phone to be of use. The UGREEN Slim, BFADEHA and SPOTMINDERS are iOS only. The Ridge, Chipolo CARD and KIUP work with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub. A card joins one network at a time. If you might switch phone type, pick a dual-network card.

A wallet is often buried in a bag or a coat, so the ring needs to carry. The KIUP lists up to 120 dB, the UGREEN Slim, BFADEHA and SPOTMINDERS list 100 dB, and the Ridge lists 95 dB with a range up to 300 feet. The Chipolo CARD gives no figure. Decibel numbers are manufacturer claims. A louder card helps if you have high-pitch hearing loss.

Wallets get rained on and dropped in puddles. The Ridge, SPOTMINDERS and KIUP list IP68, while the Chipolo CARD, UGREEN Slim and BFADEHA state no rating. IP68 is rated for full water exposure, which is more than you need for a wallet. A stated rating beats a silent listing when you commute in all weather.

A card you carry every day should be backed. The Chipolo CARD lists a 2-year warranty with free replacement through the seller. The other listings here describe no warranty. If the sealed battery fails, the whole card is lost. That makes a clear warranty more valuable than it would be for a coin-cell tag.

howWeEvaluated.title: Card thickness and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated thickness as the listings give it. The KIUP lists 0.06 inches, the SPOTMINDERS 0.07 inches and the BFADEHA 2.5 mm. We considered how each would sit in a real wallet slot, and we gave extra weight to cards that look like a normal credit card.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and charging
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at charging method and stated battery life. The Ridge lists up to 5 months, the SPOTMINDERS up to 8 months, the Chipolo CARD and UGREEN Slim up to a year, and the BFADEHA over 5 years non-rechargeable. Where a listing was silent we did not assume a figure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Network and phone support
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which phones each card supports. The Ridge, Chipolo CARD and KIUP support Find My or Find Hub, while the UGREEN Slim, BFADEHA and SPOTMINDERS are iOS only. Clear compatibility counted for the most.

howWeEvaluated.title: Alarm and durability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated ring volume and water rating. The KIUP lists up to 120 dB, the UGREEN Slim, BFADEHA and SPOTMINDERS 100 dB and the Ridge 95 dB. Ridge, SPOTMINDERS and KIUP list IP68. These are manufacturer claims, balanced against buyer feedback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each pick by what it does best, not by price or popularity. The Ridge leads overall, the UGREEN Slim on charge speed, the Chipolo CARD on warranty, the BFADEHA on no-charge simplicity, the SPOTMINDERS on iPhone IP68 and the KIUP on loudness. We did not rank on popularity or review counts.

faq.q: Which tracker card is best for most people?
faq.a: The Ridge Tracker Card is the best all-rounder because it works with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, lists IP68 and charges on Qi or MagSafe. If you want fewer charges, the UGREEN Slim lists up to a year, and the BFADEHA needs none. Match the tag to your phone's network before comparing anything else.

faq.q: Will a tracker card fit in my wallet?
faq.a: Most will, but they are thicker than a normal credit card. The KIUP lists 0.06 inches, the SPOTMINDERS 0.07 inches and the BFADEHA 2.5 mm. If your wallet is already tight, try one in the slot before depending on it.

faq.q: Do I need a special charger?
faq.a: Rechargeable cards charge wirelessly. The Ridge uses any Qi or MagSafe charger, and the Chipolo CARD needs a Qi magnetic charger that is not included. Check what your listing says before buying, and plan to own a pad.

faq.q: What happens when the sealed battery runs out?
faq.a: You usually replace the whole card. The BFADEHA is listed for over 5 years and the KIUP claims 5 to 10 years, but those are manufacturer numbers. The Chipolo CARD has a 2-year warranty that may cover early failure. Ask the seller if you rely on a warranty.

faq.q: Is a tracker card the same as a GPS tracker?
faq.a: No, and this is the most common misconception. A card rings over Bluetooth when you are near and relies on passing phones to report a last known location. It does not give live GPS. It is meant for finding a wallet, not tracking a person.

faq.q: Can a card track me without my knowing?
faq.a: Certified trackers are designed to trigger unknown tracker alerts on phones, which protects privacy. If you see an alert, follow the on-screen steps. Never place a card in another person's belongings without consent.
